task: CS2 human-like Deathmatch bot — math/algorithms for simultaneous movement + shooting; then seamless attention blending, kinematic extrapolation, async Rust+ort architecture (issue #3)

tech_stack.navigation_yaw_pitch_predictor: RepViT M1.5 (returns spatial coords + yaw/pitch on maps)
tech_stack.execution_providers: CUDA / TensorRT for RepViT and YOLO

hypothesis_tree.claim: Human aiming is decomposable into a primary ballistic submovement + corrective submovements (Meyer/Crossman-Goodeve / WHo model).
supporting: Meyer 1988 'Optimality in human motor performance' iso-vu model
Bullock & Grossberg VITE
Plamondon delta-lognormal Sigma-Lognormal model
hypothesis_tree.consequences: We can synthesize aim curves as a sum of overlapping bell-shaped speed profiles (Sigma-Lognormal); produces both ballistic + corrective phases.

hypothesis_tree.claim: Mouse path geometry is well modelled by Bezier curves perturbed by Perlin/OU noise with constant-jerk timing.
supporting: Bezmouse / pyclick / GhostCursor / WindMouse algorithm by Benjamin J. Land (Aldaron) 2007
Minimum-jerk model Flash & Hogan 1985
hypothesis_tree.consequences: Use 3rd-order Bezier between current and target with noise overlay; reparameterize time with min-jerk profile.

hypothesis_tree.claim: Counter-strafe accuracy mechanic in CS2 is the dominant constraint on simultaneous movement+shooting.
supporting: Valve developer wiki on weapon_accuracy_nospread / inaccuracy
CS2 movement inaccuracy decay constants from cs_weapon_data
hypothesis_tree.consequences: Bot must press opposite key for ~50–80 ms before shooting (A then D, etc.) to zero velocity, then re-press.

hypothesis_tree.claim: PID/Kalman fusion of RepViT yaw/pitch (low-frequency, prior) with YOLO target offsets (high-frequency, evidence) yields stable aim.
supporting: Standard sensor-fusion / Kalman Filter literature; complementary filter alternative
hypothesis_tree.consequences: Treat RepViT as process model, YOLO measurement; tune Q/R to taste.

hypothesis_tree.claim: Reaction-time noise (200–250 ms median) and overshoot ratio (~5–10 %) must be sampled to defeat anti-cheat heuristics and bot-detection by ML.
supporting: Reaction-time meta-analyses; ex-Gaussian distribution
hypothesis_tree.consequences: Sample reaction delay from ex-Gaussian (mu, sigma, tau) before triggering aim+fire.

hypothesis_tree.claim: Seamless transition between RepViT path-following authority and YOLO enemy-flicking authority is achieved by an asymmetric one-pole saliency envelope feeding a smootherstep weight that drives slerp between two critically-damped quaternion attitudes; squad generalizes to >=3 authorities.
supporting: Shoemake 1985 SIGGRAPH — Animating rotation with quaternion curves (slerp definition)
Perlin 2002 SIGGRAPH course 'Improving Noise' — smootherstep S2(t)=6t^5-15t^4+10t^3 with vanishing 1st and 2nd derivatives
Tanaka et al. 1998 Neuroscience Research 32:197 — saccade-to-pursuit transition latency and gain enhancement
Orban de Xivry & Lefevre 2013 Frontiers in Systems Neuroscience 7:4 — saccade/pursuit interaction review
Daniel Holden 'Spring-It-On' (theorangeduck.com/page/spring-roll-call) — closed-form, dt-independent critically damped spring with half-life parameterization
Earlevel one-pole filter / asymmetric envelope generator references (audio dynamics canonical form)
Lisberger & Westbrook 1985 — presaccadic-to-postsaccadic pursuit gain enhancement
Land & Tatler 2009 'Looking and Acting' OUP — saccadic suppression
hypothesis_tree.consequences: Blender pipeline = (raw detection event) -> attack/release one-pole on saliency alpha with tau_a~30ms, tau_r~250ms -> smootherstep -> slerp(q_path_smoothed, q_enemy_smoothed, S2(alpha)); each attitude pre-filtered by a half-life~25ms critically damped angular spring; attenuate YOLO contribution to saliency by exp(-|omega|/omega0) during in-flight flicks (saccadic suppression analogue).

hypothesis_tree.claim: RepViT's spatial-pose output is stale by one inference window; the right correction is bias-correction extrapolation in which the bot's engine velocity drives the forward prediction and RepViT contributes only a slowly-varying drift residual; for retro-fitting between two anchors use cubic Hermite; for intent-drift handling use projective velocity blending; for the formal canonical form follow IEEE 1278.1 DRM(F,P,W).
supporting: IEEE 1278.1-2012 Distributed Interactive Simulation — Application Protocols, Dead-Reckoning Models DRM(F,P,W) and DRM(F,V,W) (constant-velocity, constant-acceleration, with/without rotation)
Eric Lengyel 2010 'Game Engine Gems 1' chapter on Projective Velocity Blending — blends predicted server position with current client extrapolation along a projective curve to avoid pop-in
Wikipedia 'Cubic Hermite spline' — basis functions h00, h10, h01, h11 used for C1 retro-fits between two pose anchors
Kalman 1960 — A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction Problems (used as conceptual frame for the bias-correction filter)
Aaron Aronov (Riot Games / GDC) talks on net-code dead reckoning
Walker 2008 thesis on networked simulation extrapolation (referenced in Lengyel chapter)
hypothesis_tree.consequences: Predicted view at controller time t_now = base RepViT pose + integrate(engine velocity, dt_lag) - bias_term, where bias_term is a slow EMA of (RepViT estimate - own integrated track) at past common timestamps. Use cubic Hermite for one-shot retro-correction between previous prediction and new authoritative pose so the controller's input is C1-continuous.

hypothesis_tree.claim: Async ONNX inference threads should share state with the 1 kHz control loop using wait-free SPSC primitives — triple_buffer for fast-changing perception snapshots, ArcSwap for slow-changing config — with one ort::Session per inference thread driving Session::run_async on its own intra-op thread pool, controller pinned with SCHED_FIFO and paced by spin_sleep.
supporting: pykeio ort crate docs (ort.pyke.io / docs.rs/ort) — Session::run_async, SessionBuilder::with_intra_threads, with_parallel_execution, ExecutionProvider::CUDA/TensorRT
HadrienG2/triple_buffer crate — wait-free SPSC triple buffer (always read latest, never block writer)
vorner/arc-swap crate — wait-free reads of an Arc, RCU-style swap-on-update for slow-changing data
alexheretic/spin_sleep crate — accurate sub-millisecond sleep on Windows/Linux
ONNX Runtime documentation on intra_op_num_threads vs inter_op_num_threads
Linux man sched(7) on SCHED_FIFO; Windows SetThreadPriority(THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL)
DPDK / audio-callback / game-engine literature on lock-free real-time threads
hypothesis_tree.consequences: Architecture has three threads: (a) RepViT inference thread owns ort::Session_repvit and writes to TripleBuffer<RepVitFrame>; (b) YOLO inference thread owns ort::Session_yolo and writes to TripleBuffer<YoloFrame>; (c) Controller thread (SCHED_FIFO/TIME_CRITICAL) reads both triple buffers and an ArcSwap<Config>, runs the blender + extrapolator + counter-strafe FSM, and emits HID events. No locks on the hot path; all sessions use Session::run_async to overlap GPU dispatch with controller ticks.
